description: CRIT-005's description text cites 'PROP-201a-i' as within its scope ('REQ-201/203, PROP-201a-i, PROP-201g', contract line 86), which literally includes PROP-201i (the hl_trade lazy/fail-open query behavior). CRIT-006 separately and specifically grades PROP-201i via its own concrete passThreshold ('matching PROP-201i(a)/(b)/(c)'s three named tests', contract line 120). This leaves PROP-201i nominally graded under two different CRIT items with no stated precedence, contrary to this review's own requirement that contract criteria be 'non-overlapping.' In this specific case the ambiguity is low-risk because CRIT-006's passThreshold is the one with concrete, checkable substance (the deliberately-induced-failure test), while CRIT-005's passThreshold text does not actually re-test PROP-201i's specifics -- so no real double-grading occurs in practice. But the textual overlap is still a structural defect: a future negotiation round could plausibly claim PROP-201i is 'covered' by CRIT-005 alone (which does not concretely test it) while skipping CRIT-006's concrete checks, or vice versa treat the two as redundant and drop one.
